## Dynamic Prompts Text Box

Supports dynamic prompt syntax and wildcards for flexible prompt generation.

**Documentation:**  
[SD Dynamic Prompts Guide](https://github.com/adieyal/sd-dynamic-prompts/tree/main)

**Usage:**
- Use dynamic prompt syntax/wildcards for advanced prompting
- Or write standard prompts directly—dynamic features are optional

**Alternative Setup:**
If you don't need dynamic prompts or prefer not to install custom nodes, replace the node DynamicPrompts Text Box (Positive Prompt) with the standard **CLIP Text Encode** node and connect it to the positive conditioning input on the **WAN ImageToVideo** node.

# ⚠️ DISABLE (Ctrl+B) LOAD IMAGE NODE ABOVE WHEN USING THIS ⚠️

## Batch Image Loader

Automatically loads images sequentially from a folder with each execution.

**Setup Instructions:**
- Set **Int value** to `0`
- Set **control** to `increment`
- Specify **source folder** path (containing your images)
- Configure **Dimensions** as needed

**Usage:**
If your folder contains 16 images, simply run the workflow 16 times. The counter increments automatically with each run, loading the next image in sequence. No manual loading required.

**If not needed:**
Disable via Fast Groups Bypasser and enable the usual **Load Image** node.

nodes.title: How to use the workflow
widgets_values:
This workflow is a 3 in 1 combination of my previous, seperate workflows. I was getting tired of loading different workflows all the time. It features on and off switches for the desired workflow branch with it's own Power LoRA Loaders. Video model, speed LoRAs, Vae and Clip is loaded and set in the Control Center. The video output is on the far right. Adjust your desired save-video path accordingly.

⚠️

Important: Models go into these folders inside your ComfyUI-Installation:
- model files like SmoothMix or other Wan 2.2 models go to models/diffusion_models
- LoRAs go to models/LoRAs
- VAE goes to models/vae
- Clip goes to models/text_encoders

⚠️

# How to use the workflow

## 1. Control Center

Here you specify the desired video parameters and load your video models and speed LoRAs. **You have to update the node paths to the location of the files on your drive.** To do so simply click the model name and choose the model from the dropdown menu. If you don't do that, the models won't load correctly.

The Unet Loader (GGUF) loads GGUF models. Disable or enable **(Ctrl+B)** depending on which kind of model you're using.

**Important note about steps:**
- Steps sets the amount of total steps (e.g. 6 or 8)
- Second steps is the step count you want the model to switch from High to Low Sampling. If you want to render your video using 8 steps you could set Steps to 8 and Second Steps to 4. That way, it would split the Steps 4/4. You could also set second steps to 3 to split at 3/5.

Speed LoRAs are also set in the Control Center. See the links at the bottom of this guide if you want to download the speed LoRAs I use.

**For FP8 scaled I generally use:**

**on High:**
- Wan_2_2_I2V_A14B_HIGH_lightx2v_MoE_distill_lora_rank64_bf16 @ 0.50 - 1.50 (but you can go up as high as 3.00) Try what works best on your system.

**on Low:**
- lightx2v_I2V_14B_480p_cfg_step_distill_rank128_bf16 @ 1.50

**For GGUF I use:**

**on High:**
- Wan21_I2V_14B_lightx2v_cfg_step_distill_lora_rank64 @ 3.00

**on Low:**
- Wan21_I2V_14B_lightx2v_cfg_step_distill_lora_rank64 @ 1.50

But feel free to try other Speed LoRAs. They might give you different results depending on your system.

Video model and speed LoRAs get set as the used model and feed into a set node. So no need to wire anything in this worklflow. Everything is set up to just set up the Control Center and then choosing the desired workflow branch.

**Important note on Interpolation and Upscaling:
You can choose to upscale and or interpolate seperately or together. Just disable what you don't need via Fast Groups Bypasser nodes.

## 2. First Last Frame

You Load the First image and the image you want the scene to end on as the last Image. Then you prompt and go for it. **You do not need to save a last frame here, because you already should have one. So disable the "Save Last Frame"-Node in the Fast Groups Bypasser.** Nothing more to say here. **Don't forget to load your LoRAs in the Power Lora Loader.**

## 3. Image 2 Video

My daily driver. Set up LoRA, load the image, prompt away and run. Easy as 1, 2, 3. Note the guide on how to use the batch image loader if you want to use all images in a specific folder for a batch run. Also note the guide on how to use Dynamic Prompt Syntax.

## 4. Loop

More or less the same as FLF (First Last Frame) but it uses the same image for start and end, thus creating a loop. **You do not need to save a last frame here, because you already should have one. So disable the "Save Last Frame"-Node in the Fast Groups Bypasser.**

## 5. Save Last Frame

Only really useful for the Image 2 Video branch. It saves the last video frame for further use in the next run. If you ever wondered how I make most of my longform videos: this is your answer.
